solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Note shortage with home missing out

indicators.note: missing out says these letters are dropped from the longer word

parts.note: a famine is a severe shortage, usually of food
'in' means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: Someone complains of being short of money with their house left out of the reckoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' is a noun here in the sense of distinction, as in 'a person of note'; 'missing out' removes IN from FAMINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to be of note is to have renown or celebrity.

clue.text: Country female has love affair, losing honour

indicators.note: losing says the honour is taken away from the affair

parts.note: a romance is a love affair
OM, the Order of Merit, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A woman embarks on an affair and forfeits her good name.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is an honour awarded by the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a European nation with Paris as its capital.

clue.text: Intellectual restricted by government always

indicators.note: restricted by says the letters are held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A thinker whose freedom is constantly curbed by the state.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: relating to the mind, the intellect.

clue.text: Formula for hospital room creates disadvantage

indicators.note: formula for says the answer is a recipe whose working produces the words that follow

parts.note: a hospital room is a ward; read as an instruction, the answer says take 'draw' and turn it back, which spells ward

explanation.surface: A plan for arranging a hospital room turns out to have a snag.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: 'Formula for' says the answer, read as an instruction, is the recipe that produces WARD, a hospital room.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a snag or downside is a disadvantage.

clue.text: Dirty job son gets stuck into

indicators.note: gets stuck into puts the son inside the job

parts.note: a duty is a job or task

explanation.surface: A dirty job the son gets stuck into.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: covered in grime or dust means dirty.

clue.text: At sea pirate had a wicked form of rule

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are in disorder

explanation.surface: A pirate on the ocean held cruel sway.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: South Africa's system of racial segregation was an unjust regime.

clue.text: East and West uniting in common purpose?

definitions.text: East and West uniting in common purpose?

parts.words: East and West uniting in common purpose?
parts.note: looks like diplomacy between nations, but in the card game the players sitting East and West play as a team

explanation.surface: A hopeful picture of East and West cooperating on the world stage.
explanation.walkthrough: In the card game, the four players are named by compass points, and opposite players partner each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: in the card game, the players called East and West form a partnership.

clue.text: Prisoner given extra punishment and not let out?

parts.note: con is slang for a convict, a prisoner
fined means given a monetary penalty

explanation.surface: A prisoner receives further penalties and is denied release.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: kept shut in, enclosed, means not allowed out.

clue.text: A girl's dissent's possibly an indication that urgent help is needed

definitions.text: an indication that urgent help is needed

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: the word with its S counted as a letter
the word with its S counted as a letter

explanation.surface: A young woman's protest might be a cry for help.
explanation.walkthrough: Both apostrophe S endings count as letters in the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an SOS or a flare is a call for rescue.

clue.text: First drop of alcohol loosens up family members

indicators.note: the first drop of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: to untie something is to loosen it, undoing a knot

explanation.surface: A first sip of drink relaxes the relatives at a family gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: aunts, a parent's sisters, are relatives within the family.

clue.text: In a row as the result of dodgy dealing

indicators.note: dodgy dealing is crooked, so the letters of the word are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A quarrel breaks out because of shady business dealings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a row' tempts as a quarrel, but it means lined up.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: things set in a straight line are lined up together.

clue.text: Worries about being sadder after mishap

indicators.note: after a mishap things are jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone frets about feeling sadder following an accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to fear anxiously, as a verb, is to be worried.

clue.text: A new attempt to join church and chapel

indicators.note: to join says the new attempt is attached to the church abbreviation, which comes first in the answer

parts.note: a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A fresh bid to bring a church and its chapel together.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a chantry is a chapel endowed for priests to sing masses for a founder's soul.

clue.text: End of joke that could bring a tingle

indicators.note: could bring suggests the letters might be made into something else by rearrangement

explanation.surface: A punchline so good it sends a shiver of pleasure through the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the punchline that ends a joke is its tag line.

clue.text: New car presented in magazine feature

indicators.note: new signals the letters are made over into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A magazine shows off a new model of car.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the middle double-page spread is a showpiece feature of a magazine.

clue.text: Passing rain's unfortunately penetrating shelter

indicators.note: penetrating puts the jumbled rain inside the shelter

parts.note: a tent is a shelter

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests the letters have come out wrong, in a jumble

explanation.surface: Passing showers sadly leak into the campers' tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' scrambles the rain's letters, and 'penetrating' sends that jumble inside the shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: short-lived or fleeting describes what is passing.

clue.text: Cabin in Switzerland on a lease

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the first piece above the next

parts.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland
to let is to lease

explanation.surface: A holiday cabin in the Alps rented out on a lease.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a wooden Swiss house or holiday hut is a cabin.

clue.text: Empty-headed and ranting stupidly about nothing

indicators.note: about means surrounding, the jumbled letters going round the zero
stupidly signals the letters are put in a foolish order

parts.note: nothing is zero, written as O

explanation.surface: Someone empty-headed is raving foolishly about nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupidly' makes IGNRANT from RANTING, then 'about' puts it round O.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lacking knowledge is being uninformed, empty of learning.

clue.text: Flag that's raised aloft to denote excellence

definitions.meaning: a standard is a flag, and one flown up top is high
a very good level of quality, as in 'work of a top level'

explanation.surface: A flag hoisted high to signal top quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a high level of quality is excellence.

clue.text: Duck, a swimmer lacking elegance?

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of zero, written as O
a fish is a swimmer

explanation.surface: A duck as a swimmer is clumsy and graceless.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: clumsy and boorish behaviour is the opposite of grace.

clue.text: Soldiers once more ignoring one former President

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

indicators.note: ignoring says the one is left out

parts.note: again means once more
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Troops again disregard a one-time head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers are a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Ronald, the US leader of the 1980s, was a president.

clue.text: Stories about love and about people soft in the head?

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, the fibs going round the other letters

parts.note: stories in the sense of untruths are lies
love is zero in tennis, written as O
on means about, as in 'a talk on birds'

explanation.surface: Tales concerning romance and about simple-minded folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' does two jobs: first it means surrounding, then it is a synonym for on.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: crazy or foolish people, the dim-witted, are called this slang term.

clue.text: Staff appointment gets approval

parts.note: to staff a post is to man it
a date is an arranged appointment

explanation.surface: An employee's appointment to a post is signed off.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a mandate is an authority or approval given, as by voters to a government.

clue.text: Ways to be self-effacing for the most part

indicators.note: for the most part means only most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: modest means self-effacing

explanation.surface: Ways to be humble most of the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: manners or methods of doing things are ways.

clue.text: Even one with skill may suffer setback as a novice

indicators.note: a setback sends things backwards, so the whole sequence is turned back to front

parts.note: e'en is the poetic contraction of even
one is I, the Roman numeral
art is skill, as in 'the art of persuasion'

explanation.surface: Even a skilled person may hit a setback when starting out as a beginner.
explanation.walkthrough: EEN + I + ART read backwards gives the answer; 'Even' as a poetic E'EN is the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone still learning a job is a beginner, a newcomer.

clue.text: Pet is bold, jumping across lake

indicators.note: jumping across pictures the bold word leaping over and enclosing the lake

parts.note: daring means bold
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A dog leaps boldly over a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a pet, in the sense of a favourite or beloved one, is a dear.

clue.text: Fashions worn by Italian holy men of old

indicators.note: worn by puts the Italian inside the fashions, as clothes enclose their wearer

parts.note: styles are fashions

explanation.surface: Clothes in the latest fashions modelled by an Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: Fashions worn by someone surround that person, which is why the Italian goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: early Christian ascetics who lived on top of pillars, such as Simeon, are this kind of saint.

clue.text: Feature of country with eastern area destroyed

indicators.note: eastern points to the right-hand end of the word in an across entry
destroyed says the area letter is wiped out

parts.note: China is a country

explanation.surface: A feature of a nation whose eastern region has been laid waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the jaw's front point is one of the facial features.
